summary.headline: A week behind target: orders at 87.4% and revenue at 87.5%, with the new quarter and year both opening below target and cancellations rising a third week.

points.what: Orders reached 87.4% of the weekly target and revenue 87.5%.
points.so_what: The quarter opens behind target, so the gap has to be recovered in the weeks that follow.

points.what: Orders fell 5.7% week on week to 681 and revenue fell 6.1%, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Volume and value moved away from the weekly target rather than toward it.

points.what: Orders were up 51.3% on last year and revenue up 48.9%, against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth on last year is real but slower than the rate the targets are built on, which is why the week lands behind.

points.what: New customer signups rose 12.5% week on week, a change flagged as notable and rated good.
points.so_what: Signups moved up while orders moved down, so the two measures point in opposite directions this week.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose for a third consecutive week, from 13.0% to 16.0%.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth $563 of revenue, so a trend that is not reversing keeps weighing on weekly revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 15 Dec 2025 rose 1.6 pp, a change flagged as notable, and was 3.2 pp above last year.
points.so_what: Returns are moving in the bad direction against both the prior week and last year, so this is not a one-off comparison effect.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target requires $73,875 of revenue a week, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $49,177.
points.so_what: At the current pace the full-year target is out of reach.

points.what: Orders finished 98 below the weekly target and revenue $6,736 below.
points.so_what: The miss is on both volume and value, with neither offsetting the other.

points.what: QTD revenue is 87.5% of target, with $727,233 still needed against the full-quarter target of $774,555.
points.so_what: Almost the entire quarterly target rests on the 12 weeks still to come.

points.what: YTD revenue is 87.5% of target, leaving $3,841,480 of the $3,888,802 full-year target outstanding.
points.so_what: The year starts from behind, so later weeks have to run above target to recover the shortfall.

points.what: North America orders fell 20.2% to 130, contributing 33 of the week's order decline, or 80.5% of the change.
points.so_what: Most of the decline sits in one region rather than being spread across the business.

points.what: Search orders fell 7.2% to 487, contributing 38 orders, or 92.7% of the week's change.
points.so_what: The weekly order trend is set mainly by Search rather than by the smaller sources.

points.what: Organic orders rose 13.6% to 100, adding 12 orders, and LATAM added 4.
points.so_what: The gains were too small to offset the declines elsewhere, so the total still fell.

points.what: AOV was $82.73, flat week on week but down 3.2% on last year, and flagged as outside its 8-week range.
points.so_what: Revenue growth on last year is coming from more orders rather than bigger baskets.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 16.0%, up 0.3 pp on last week but 1.3 pp below the same week last year.
points.so_what: Order quality is worse than last week while still better than a year ago, so the yearly comparison reads better than the current trend.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate was 10.3% in the mature week of 15 Dec 2025, against 8.7% the week before.
points.so_what: Two order-quality measures are now moving in the bad direction at the same time.

points.what: New signups were 252, up 10.5% on last year, while orders were up 51.3%.
points.so_what: Order growth on last year is running well ahead of the growth in new accounts.

summary.headline: Week 1 of Q1 came in behind target on both orders and revenue at 87.4% and 87.5%, and the year opens behind at 87.5% attainment.

points.what: Orders were 681 against a target of 779, an attainment of 87.4%, a gap of 98 orders.
points.so_what: The quarter starts with a shortfall to make up in its remaining 12 weeks.

points.what: Revenue was $47,322, or 87.5% of the $54,058 weekly target.
points.so_what: Because QTD and YTD both cover only this week, the whole year now reads at 87.5% attainment.

points.what: Orders fell 5.7% week on week and revenue fell 6.1%, both rated bad.
points.so_what: The week moved away from target rather than towards it, with next week's bar set higher at 810 orders and $58,234.

points.what: Orders were up 51.3% and revenue up 48.9% on the same week last year, both rated good, against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Year-on-year growth is real but below the pace the targets were built on, which is why the week still missed.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose for a third consecutive week, from 13.0% to 16.0%.
points.so_what: A third straight move in the bad direction means the cancellation trend is not reversing, and each percentage point carries $563 of revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 15 Dec 2025 was 10.3%, up 1.6 pp, a change the brief marks as notable and rated bad.
points.so_what: Returns are moving in the wrong direction on top of cancellations, so more of the week's gross revenue is at risk of coming back.

points.what: Reaching the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $73,875 of revenue a week, against a current 8-week run-rate of $49,177.
points.so_what: The required pace sits far above the recent pace, so at this rate the full-year target is out of reach.

points.what: Orders reached 87.4% of target and revenue 87.5%, both behind, with a revenue gap of $6,736.
points.so_what: Both halves of the week missed, so the shortfall is in volume rather than in order value.

points.what: QTD revenue stands at 87.5% of target, with $727,233 still needed against the full-quarter target of $774,555 over 12 weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter opens behind, so later weeks have to run above target to close the gap.

points.what: The full year needs $73,875 a week, while the recent 8-week run-rate is $49,177 and this week delivered $47,322.
points.so_what: Current output sits well below what the year requires, so the January MTD position remains the only month recorded and it is behind target.

points.what: North America fell 20.2% to 130 orders, contributing 33 of the 41-order decline, or 80.5% of the change.
points.so_what: Most of the week's miss against the orders target sits in one region.

points.what: Search fell 7.2% to 487 orders, contributing 38 orders, or 92.7% of the total change.
points.so_what: With 71.5% of orders in one source, movement in Search decides whether the weekly target is met.

points.what: Organic rose 13.6% to 100 orders, adding 12 orders, and LATAM rose 4.2% to 99 orders.
points.so_what: These gains were not large enough to offset the declines elsewhere, so total orders still finished below target.

points.what: AOV was $82.73, flat week on week but down 3.2% on last year, rated bad, and outside its 8-week range.
points.so_what: With AOV no higher than last week, the revenue decline traces back to fewer orders.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 16.0%, up 0.3 pp and rated bad, though down 1.3 pp on last year, which is rated good.
points.so_what: The year-on-year comparison is favourable while the recent direction is not, so the weekly trend is the one to follow.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 15 Dec 2025 was 10.3%, up 3.2 pp on last year, rated bad.
points.so_what: Order quality is weaker than a year ago on the returns measure, even as order volumes grow.

points.what: New signups rose 12.5% to 252, a notable increase, and were up 10.5% on last year, both rated good.
points.so_what: Signups moved up in a week when orders fell, the only headline measure to improve against last week.
